title: Unit 7 Stand-alone 6: Aminoglycoside - Renal Function Labs

question.stem: Which of the following laboratory test results should the nurse review before administering the medication?

options.text: serum electrolyte level and serum uric acid level
hemoglobin (Hgb) and white blood cell (WBC) count
serum ammonia level and serum glucose level
blood urea nitrogen (BUN) and serum creatinine

question.footnote: © NCSBN. Taken from https://www.nclex.com/prepare.page; click on 'Download Exam Preview'.
question.preamble: The nurse is preparing to administer an aminoglycoside.
question.explanation: Aminoglycosides are nephrotoxic, so the nurse should review blood urea nitrogen (BUN) and serum creatinine (Option 4) before administration to confirm adequate renal function and avoid drug accumulation and toxicity. Serum electrolyte and uric acid levels (Option 1), hemoglobin and WBC count (Option 2), and serum ammonia and glucose levels (Option 3) are not the primary safety labs associated with aminoglycoside nephrotoxicity.
